message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"9.18","text":"How many also falsely allege oracles and healings accomplished by them, and affirm these healings with oaths? How many have hired themselves out for pay, undertaking through certain contrivances to suffer some ailment and proclaiming it as such; then, after being restored from their ailment by a counteracting influence, they say that the treatment was prescribed by oracle, so that they may credit the insensible object of worship? How many of these objects of worship were consecrated from the outset by magical art, so that each might ὑνερπολῇ and deliver oracles? And yet, after a long time, these too failed. How many now practice sorcery because they want to strengthen such things? Nevertheless, something is not a god merely because it can foretell the future or bring healing.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"καὶ ταύτας βεβαιοῦνται μετὰ ὅρκων","chosen":"and affirm these healings with oaths","rationale":"The feminine plural ταύτας most directly refers to the immediately preceding θεραπείας, “healings,” rather than broadening the object to include the oracle claims."},{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ μισθῷ ἑαυτοὺς ἐξέδωκαν","chosen":"have hired themselves out for pay","rationale":"The expression describes placing oneself at another’s disposal in return for payment."},{"source_quote":"δι’ ἐνίων ἐπινοιῶν πάσχειν τινὰ ἀναδεξάμενοι","chosen":"undertaking through certain contrivances to suffer some ailment","rationale":"ἐπίνοιαι are devised schemes or contrivances, while τινά is understood as the indefinite suffering or symptoms they undertake to exhibit. A less likely syntactic alternative takes τινά as certain persons who are made to suffer."},{"source_quote":"ἀντιπαθείᾳ ἀποκατασταθέντες","chosen":"after being restored from their ailment by a counteracting influence","rationale":"ἀντιπάθεια denotes an opposing or counteracting influence, possibly treatment by contraries; the source does not specify the mechanism."},{"source_quote":"κεχρηματίσθαι τὴν θεραπείαν λέγουσιν","chosen":"they say that the treatment was prescribed by oracle","rationale":"The perfect passive infinitive presents the treatment or healing as having been announced or prescribed through an oracle."},{"source_quote":"ἵνα τὸ ἀναίσθητον ἐπιγράψωσιν σέβασμα","chosen":"so that they may credit the insensible object of worship","rationale":"In context, ἐπιγράφω concerns attributing the result or attaching credit, while the object of worship is characterized as lacking perception or sensation."},{"source_quote":"πόσα δὲ αὐτῶν","chosen":"How many of these objects of worship","rationale":"The neuter plural most naturally refers to the insensible objects of worship just mentioned, though a broader reference to the cultic phenomena remains possible."},{"source_quote":"ἐκ καταρχῆς μαγικῇ τέχνῃ ἐτελέσθη","chosen":"were consecrated from the outset by magical art","rationale":"In this cultic context τελέω can denote ritual completion or consecration; “were effected” or “were brought about” remains possible if the referent is the phenomena rather than the objects."},{"source_quote":"καὶ ὅμως μακρῷ χρόνῳ καὶ ταῦτα διεφώνησεν","chosen":"And yet, after a long time, these too failed","rationale":"διαφωνέω indicates that these eventually ceased to correspond to the claims or proved unsuccessful. A more formally literal alternative is “these too turned out otherwise over time.”"},{"source_quote":"πλὴν οὐκ εἴ τι μαντικόν ἐστιν ἢ θεραπευτικόν, τοῦτο θεός ἐστιν","chosen":"Nevertheless, something is not a god merely because it can foretell the future or bring healing","rationale":"The conditional construction denies that divinatory or healing ability establishes that something is a god."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἵνα ὑνερπολῇ καὶ χρηματίζῃ","issue":"The image-checked selected edition clearly reads ὑνερπολῇ, but this form cannot be securely identified as a regular lexeme or assigned a defensible English meaning in the purpose clause. It remains untranslated rather than being silently corrected. The conjecture ὑπερπολῇ might suggest a sense such as “gain ascendancy” or “prevail,” but that conjecture does not establish the meaning of the supplied reading and has not been substituted for it.","proposed_reading":"ἵνα ὑπερπολῇ καὶ χρηματίζῃ","blocks_publication":true}]}]}
